answer_1.quote: In this work, we treat LLMs as data generators rather than task inferencer for complex symbolic language tasks, with the generated data being used to train much affordable model for depolyment and inference.
answer_1.outputs: structured symbolic outputs such as SQL queries, Bash commands, Python programs, Prolog commands, TOP-representations, and QDMR

answer_2.quote: We determine model performance based on surface form Exact Set Match (EM; Yu et al. (2018b)) and test-suite Execution accuracy (EX; Zhong et al. (2020a))...

answer_4.quote: In order to evaluate the quality of generated data, we also present human evaluations on the data-pair quality of generated Spider and MBPP datasets. We randomly sample 100 examples from SYMGEN for both datasets and manually review the sampled data.
answer_4.guideline: We found 81 and 79 examples are correct for MBPP and Spider, respectively. ... However, there are mainly three issues that exist in the data generated by SYMGEN in both MBPP and Spider. First, SYMGEN may generate ambiguous and under-specified questions... Secondly, the answers sometimes can be meaninglessly complex... Thirdly, it can be difficult to verify the correctness...
